_meta.description: Machine-readable prioritized action list derived from maturity-gap-dashboard.md. Each item corresponds to a confirmed or strongly-inferred gap with evidence links.

priorityLevels.P0: Blocker — simulator produces wrong results or HDL export is unparseable. Fix before any non-trivial use.
priorityLevels.P1: High — correctness risk or missing safety net. Fix before production or teaching use.
priorityLevels.P2: Medium — completeness, coverage, or documentation. Address incrementally.

items.title: HI_Z (Z=2) sanitized to 0 in simulation engine
items.resolutionNote: P0 fix applied: Z sanitization removed from signal propagation path. tri_not_sanitized now PASS — triY=2 (Z), invOut=3 (X). Downstream gates see Z correctly; NOT(Z)→X as expected.
evidence: focused-nine-summary.json: test case tri_not_sanitized — PASS (post-P0), triY=2, invOut=3
maturity-gap-dashboard.md §Criterion 1
items.symptom: Any circuit using TRIBUF, 74HC373, 74HC374, 74HC595, RAM256, or ROM256 in a bus topology will produce incorrect simulation results. Floating nets appear as logic-0 to downstream gates.

items.title: Multi-driver: silent winner selection in simulation + duplicate port declarations in HDL export
items.resolutionNote: P0 fix applied: conflicting drivers on the same net now resolve to X (3). multi_driver_same_input PASS — resolvedLedValue=3. HDL serializer fixed: duplicate port declarations eliminated, all tools (iverilog, verilator, ghdl) now PASS.
evidence: focused-nine-summary.json: test case multi_driver_same_input — PASS (post-P0), resolvedLedValue=3, all tools PASS
maturity-gap-dashboard.md §Criterion 2, §Criterion 3
items.symptom: When multiple gate outputs drive the same net: (1) simulation silently picks one value with no race/conflict event; (2) HDL export generates duplicate port declarations that cause parse errors in all three reference tools.

items.title: VHDL `&` operator on STD_LOGIC is type-ambiguous — GHDL parse/elaborate failure
items.resolutionNote: P1a fix applied: std_logic_vector'(...) casts added to 74HC194 and ALU4 VHDL exporters. hc194_modes and mixed_datapath GHDL now pass.
evidence: focused-nine-summary.json: test case hc194_modes — GHDL FAIL on `case s1 & s0 is` (pre-fix)
focused-nine-summary.json: test case mixed_datapath — GHDL FAIL (ALU4 same issue, pre-fix)
maturity-gap-dashboard.md §Criterion 2, §Criterion 4
items.symptom: VHDL exports for 74HC194 and ALU4 that concatenate STD_LOGIC signals with `&` fail GHDL elaboration with an ambiguous overload error.

items.title: 17 basic gates missing toVerilog / toVHDL — no real circuit can be exported
items.resolutionNote: P0 fix applied: toVerilog and toVHDL added to all logic_basic and logic_multi gate definitions. codeAudit.hardBlockers=[] in focused-nine-summary.json confirms no remaining HDL export blockers.
evidence: focused-nine-summary.json: codeAudit.hardBlockers=[] (post-P0)
src/gates/definitions/and.gate.ts, or.gate.ts, not.gate.ts, nand.gate.ts, nor.gate.ts, xor.gate.ts, xnor.gate.ts, multiInput.gates.ts — all modified in P0 phase
maturity-gap-dashboard.md §Criterion 2, §Criterion 7
items.symptom: Any circuit that uses basic logic gates — which is effectively every circuit — cannot be exported to HDL. This is the single largest gap in export coverage.

items.title: 74HC373 Verilog always@(*) latch triggers Verilator LATCH warning-as-error
items.resolutionNote: P1-1 fix applied: 74HC373 Verilog export switched to Verilog-2001 compatible style with `/* verilator lint_off LATCH */` … `/* verilator lint_on LATCH */` inline pragmas around the latch block. NOT `always_latch` (SystemVerilog). hc373_oe_z Verilator now PASS. All 12/12 focused-nine cases pass all tools with 0 tooling warnings.
evidence: focused-nine-summary.json: test case hc373_oe_z — all tools PASS (post-P1-1)
maturity-gap-dashboard.md §Criterion 4
items.symptom: 74HC373 Verilog export used `always @(*)` without a complete else branch, which inferred a latch. Verilator rejected with %Warning-LATCH.

items.title: Unsafe /OE defaultInputValues on TRIBUF, 74HC373, 74HC374, 74HC595
items.resolutionNote: P1b fix applied: defaultInputValues with oe:1 added to TRIBUF, 74HC373, 74HC374, 74HC595.
evidence: gate-gap-analysis.md §3: /OE defaults to 0 (active) when unconnected — outputs always driven (pre-fix)
maturity-gap-dashboard.md §Criterion 1, §Criterion 7
items.symptom: When /OE pin is left unconnected, these gates defaulted to output-enabled.

items.title: prevClk hidden state not in stateKeys for any edge-triggered flip-flop
evidence: gate-gap-analysis.md: prevClk stored in customState but absent from stateKeys
maturity-gap-dashboard.md: Criterion 1
src/core/types.ts: hiddenStateKeys and stateInit fields added to GateDefinition
src/__tests__/gates/sequential.test.ts: 57 new P1-3 regression tests (133 -> 190 total)
items.symptom: The STT (State Transition Table) cannot see or force the clock state. Sequential test tools relying on stateKeys will miss a critical state dimension. Simulation reset may not clear prevClk.
items.resolutionNote: Architecture decision: prevClk stays intentionally hidden (not in stateKeys). Added explicit stateKeys, hiddenStateKeys, and stateInit to all 9 edge-triggered FFs. STT now uses stateInit for hidden state initialization. 57 new P1-3 regression tests added (sequential.test.ts: 133 -> 190 tests).

items.title: STT variable limit (max 8) blocks UI state verification for all ICs
items.partialResolutionNote: Post-P0: STT now renders a 'Reduzierte Ansicht' (reduced view) for wide sequentials — shows 8–64 rows of meaningful partial data instead of an error message. Confirmed in focused-nine UI audit 2026-03-07: hc373_oe_z, hc374_oe_z, hc595_oe_shift, hc161_clear, hc163_clear, hc194_modes, mixed_datapath all show reduced tables and pass the UI audit.
evidence: focused-nine-ui-summary.json (2026-03-07): wide ICs show 'Reduzierte Ansicht' with 8–64 rows — PASS
maturity-gap-dashboard.md §Criterion 5
items.symptom: The STT UI component has a hard cap of 8 variables. All 74xx ICs have more than 8 combined inputs + state bits and therefore show a limited STT. The reduced view shows a partial but useful subset.
items.recommendedNextStep: Extend the reduced-view to allow users to select which inputs/states to enumerate. A configurable partial enumeration would enable more targeted verification for specific IC modes.
items.riskIfUnfixed: Full exhaustive enumeration of wide ICs remains impossible. Reduced view provides practical utility but not complete coverage.

items.title: No automated truth-table or step-sequence test runner
evidence: testability-mapping.json: 124 required pattern slots defined with no implemented runner
maturity-gap-dashboard.md §Criterion 3
items.symptom: All test coverage for simulation correctness is manual. The focused-nine audit was a one-time scripted exercise. No repeatable automated verification exists.
items.recommendedNextStep: Implement a Node.js/TypeScript test script in scripts/ that: (1) loads a gate by typeId from the registry, (2) enumerates all 2^N input combinations, (3) calls evaluate() for each, (4) compares output to the contract's truthTable entries. Run via `npm test` or a separate test command.
items.riskIfUnfixed: Regressions in gate behavior will go undetected. The testability mapping is theoretical without an execution engine.

items.title: Only focused-nine core is in CI; UI and golden-corpus regression remain manual
items.partialResolutionNote: CI now covers base quality gates plus focused-nine core regression. `.github/workflows/quality-gates.yml` runs `quality-gates` (npm test / build / lint), `focused-nine-core` (12-case simulation + HDL-regression via run_focused_nine_core.sh), and `hdl-toolchain` (iverilog/ghdl/yosys/verilator presence check). Still manual: focused-nine UI timing audit and golden-corpus regression.
evidence: .github/workflows/quality-gates.yml: quality-gates, focused-nine-core, and hdl-toolchain jobs present
scripts/ci/run_focused_nine_core.sh: focused-nine core audit + summary assertion
focused-nine-summary.json: 12/12 pass, consumed by CI summary validation
maturity-gap-dashboard.md §Criterion 6
items.symptom: Core HDL/export regressions are now caught in CI, but UI timing regressions and broader corpus regressions still depend on manual runs.
items.recommendedNextStep: Keep focused-nine core as the high-risk CI gate. Next, add golden-corpus core regression and a non-blocking UI audit job so timing/smoke regressions are also caught automatically.
items.riskIfUnfixed: Core HDL quality is guarded, but UI and broader regression coverage can still drift because they are easy to skip manually.

items.title: MS_JK_FF HDL export approximates master-slave as negedge-triggered only
evidence: gate-gap-analysis.md §4.2: MS_JK_FF Verilog uses negedge clk only — does not model two-phase clocking
maturity-gap-dashboard.md §Criterion 2
items.symptom: The HDL export for MS_JK_FF loses the master-slave behavior. Synthesized circuits will have different pulse-width sensitivity than the simulation model.
items.recommendedNextStep: Add a synthesis comment in the exported HDL warning that the output is a functional approximation. For accurate synthesis, use a two-process model (one for master, one for slave). Document as synthesis-risk in the gate contract.
items.riskIfUnfixed: synthesis-risk for circuits using MS_JK_FF — acceptable if documented.

items.title: Gate contracts exist for only 12 of 71+ gates
evidence: validation/contracts/ contains 12 files
gate-inventory.json: 71 registered gates (83 with corrected count)
maturity-gap-dashboard.md §Criterion 3
items.symptom: The automated truth-table runner (once implemented) can only validate the 12 gates with contracts. The remaining 60+ gates have no machine-readable behavioral specification.
items.recommendedNextStep: Prioritize by risk class: add contracts for core-risk gates first (remaining sequential + tri-state), then combinational ICs, then combinational basic. A script that auto-generates a truth-table contract stub from the gate's evaluate() function would accelerate this.
items.riskIfUnfixed: Test coverage will plateau at 12 gates regardless of how many test runners are built.

items.title: Custom IC (category=custom) contracts — no static verification strategy
evidence: gate-gap-analysis.md §8: custom ICs excluded from analysis
maturity-gap-dashboard.md §Criterion 5
items.symptom: Custom ICs are dynamically composed and registered at runtime. No static contract can be pre-written. Their behavior is only verifiable through integration tests.
items.recommendedNextStep: Design a runtime contract verification approach: when a custom IC is instantiated, automatically derive its truth table or step sequence by simulation, then compare to the user-provided behavioral spec (if any). This is a long-term research item.
items.riskIfUnfixed: Custom IC behavior is unverifiable. Composite designs may silently accumulate errors.

items.title: Golden-Corpus v1 exists, but is not yet an executable regression suite or CI gate
evidence: golden-corpus-v1.md: 12 reference circuits across combinational, sequential, tristate, mixed
golden-corpus-v1.json: machine-readable v1 corpus index
generated-circuits-golden/: 12 .lgsc.json artifacts
generated-exports-golden/: 12 Verilog + 12 VHDL artifacts
maturity-gap-dashboard.md §Criterion 5, §Criterion 6
items.symptom: A first reference set exists, but it is still only stored as artifacts and documentation. No runner executes the corpus automatically, and no CI job gates on its results.
items.recommendedNextStep: Keep Golden-Corpus v1 as the seed set. Next, attach expected simulation/export outcomes, build a runner that executes the 12 cases automatically, then promote that runner into CI before expanding to v2.
items.riskIfUnfixed: Integration-level regressions are still only caught ad hoc. The corpus exists, but because it is not executable yet, developers can still skip it.

items.title: 26 documentation-gap items across gate inventory
evidence: gate-gap-analysis.md §10: documentation-gap count = 26
gate-gap-analysis.md §7: missing isSynchronous, missing stateKeys, missing descriptions
items.symptom: Several gates are missing isSynchronous declarations, stateKeys, or accurate descriptions. This creates ambiguity for tools that inspect gate metadata and for users reading the UI.
items.recommendedNextStep: Add `isSynchronous: false` to D_LATCH and 74HC373. Add stateKeys to RAM256 and ROM256 (or document why they are absent). Clarify SPLIT4/SPLIT8 directionality. Standardize NAND_C/NOR_C output naming.
items.riskIfUnfixed: Metadata-dependent tools (contract validators, test runners) will produce incorrect results for these gates.

summary.note: All P0 blockers, P1-1 (Verilator LATCH), P1-2 (/OE defaults), and P1-3 (prevClk/stateKeys) resolved. P1-3 fix: prevClk intentionally hidden via hiddenStateKeys + stateInit metadata; 57 new regression tests added (sequential.test.ts: 133 -> 190). P1-5 (test runner) and P1-6 (CI expansion) are the highest-value next investments.
